life: A Scraping family's student (withFamily(newLifeConfig(), 'scraping'), seed r3-tax-scraping, tests/evidence3-home.test.ts's), her coursework left to the clock: dismissed 10 December 2027, her 2027 return owing the IRS $1,700.39 and Connecticut $585.33 (two terms' taxable living-expense scholarship and a year's work-study, nothing withheld). Her 2026 return owes Connecticut $3.35 alone. In February 2028 she moves her money into a Chase CD (bank.transfer, bank.open_term) and files 2027 with nothing to pay it from; bank.break_term is how she pays later. A CD's money is outside what payFromBank and a levy reach.

rows.player: Papers > Tax Returns > the year's panel > Who It's Owed To > Owed To Connecticut DRS: Pay Connecticut (Blank Pays It All) and Pay.
rows.path: Gated 'tax.pay_state' in WhoIsOwed (PapersWorkspace.tsx:108) → run('tax.pay_state', {state, year, amount?}) → statetax.ts onCommand 'tax.pay_state' → applyStatePayment. Reached by the interface: yes, drawn whenever the state side has owed.
rows.preconditions: A filed year (or a year DRS assessed) with stateDue[state].owed; amount > 0 and no more than stateOwedOn now; the bank (checking, then savings) covers it.
rows.costs: The amount, from checking then savings (payFromBank, all or nothing). No time.
rows.timing: Immediate. What's owed is accrued to the minute: Connecticut's 10% once past the due date and 1% of the tax per month or part (30.4375-day months).
rows.refusals: 'You owe Connecticut DRS nothing on that year.'; 'Pay something.'; '$X is owed to Connecticut DRS; pay that or less.'; '$X is more than the bank can cover.'
rows.outcomes: A payment split in Connecticut's order: penalty, interest, then tax (12-39h), kept on sd.payments; the ledger posts the amount from checking; paid in full: owed cleared, its STATE_NOTICE (bill, notice of intent, levy) canceled, its lien Paid with the release notice, a state plan in force ended paid.
rows.readers: stateOwedOn/owedToState (Papers, Home's Your Affairs, budget's owedEverywhere), the notice handler (STATE_NOTICE_KIND, stops when !owed), stateLienPaid → lien_release, statePlanRefusal, pastDueTo (refund offsets).
rows.persistence: returns[year].stateDue[state] (parts, owed, payments, lien) and the ledger, in the save; reload keeps the payment once (tests reload after paying).
rows.gap: Before: stale claim plus evidence missing. The row said verified on non-student lives and a fixture student. Since 2026-10-14 it is reachable by play: the Scraping life owes Connecticut $585.33 on 2027. Evidence was missing for the student and for the bank-short refusal. A defect was found on the way: Connecticut's bill, lien and notice of intent came before the tax was due (collection counted from filing).
rows.acceptance: tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts 'PLAYER JOURNEY: a part refused in March with her money in the CD; on 25 June ...' And 'filed on 1 February unpaid, Connecticut's bill waits for the 18 April due date ...' (clock): bill at due+30 days, $649.71; lien at due+60, $655.56. And 'her Connecticut plan in force ... the rest paid by Pay on Papers' (render + clock): the plan ends paid.

rows.player: Papers > Tax Returns > a filed year's panel: Amend The Return…, then File The Amendment.
rows.path: Plain button (shut with amendRefusal's title) → Gated 'tax.amend' (PapersWorkspace.tsx:282) → taxreturn.ts 'tax.amend' → TAX_AMEND_KIND in ten weeks.
rows.preconditions: A return she filed herself, within three years of filing or two of paying, none in process, and figuresFor(year) now differing from what was filed.
rows.refusals: 'There’s no return for that year.'; 'It isn’t filed: file it.'; 'The IRS filed this one…'; 'An amended return for the year is with the IRS.'; 'The time to amend it ran out on …'; 'Your return as filed matches what’s on record: there’s nothing to amend.'
rows.outcomes: amended[] with each authority's change; on processing more tax with interest from the due date, joining or defaulting a plan, or less tax off what's owed and refunded with the IRS's interest; each state by amendState.
rows.readers: owedAll, plan newLiability, ledger refund postings, yearOf(now).interest.
rows.gap: Genuinely unreachable in play. Every writer to a year's record (recordWages, recordInterest, recordScholarship, recordBenefit, recordPension, school.ts's withholding) writes at the moment it pays into that moment's year, and a year's return is raised on 1 February of the next, so a filed year's figures never change. Played: her filed 2026 and 2027 stay matched while 2028's CD interest ($836.72) lands after filing. Evidence for its processing exists only on lives with W-2s set by hand (tests/tax-lifecycle.test.ts, tests/finance-paths.test.ts, tests/defects-g8-8.test.ts).
rows.acceptance: tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts 'tax.amend: her filed 2026 and 2027 match the record, and a year more on the clock leaves them so' (command + clock): the refusal before and after a year, 2027's figures byte-identical, 2028's interest recorded.

rows.player: Papers > Tax Returns > the year's panel > the lien: Ask For Its Withdrawal As Filed In Error.
rows.preconditions: lienInError: her own return replaced an assessment and came to no more than the tax paid before the lien was filed.
rows.timing: Decided after the state's error days (Connecticut 30, SLATE's).
rows.refusals: 'It secured tax owed when it was filed: it’s released once that’s paid, not withdrawn.'; 'Asked: decided by …'; 'It’s been withdrawn.'; 'There’s no lien on that to dispute.'
rows.outcomes: Withdrawn, its fee off what's owed or back to the bank.
rows.gap: Genuinely unreachable for Connecticut, the only state a life files in: DRS assesses a non-filer from the return's own figures, so her return in its place leaves the tax as it was; Connecticut takes a payment to the penalty and interest before the tax, and files its lien only while something is owed, so the tax is never all paid before its lien is filed. Shown by play on both of her Connecticut liens: 2027's (filed at the notice of intent) and 2026's (on DRS's assessment, replaced by her own return, paid by levy). The control stays drawn, shut with its reason; whether to keep it on a Connecticut lien is the owner's decision.
rows.acceptance: tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts: the 25 June journey (disabled with its reason; refused after payment) and 'a year Connecticut levied and was paid by the levy doesn’t refuse her a plan …' (2026's assessed lien refused).

rows.path: Gated 'tax.federal_lien_withdraw' (LienPanels.tsx:105), drawn only where r.lien exists → taxreturn.ts.
rows.preconditions: A notice of federal tax lien, filed at the LT11 where $10,000 or more is owed on the year (FEDERAL_LIEN.threshold).
rows.refusals: 'There’s no federal tax lien on that year.' and the others in federalLienWithdrawRefusal.
rows.gap: Genuinely unreachable: a student's year owes the IRS under two thousand dollars ($1,700.39 for 2027, $1,746.41 at its LT11 on 20 June 2028), against the $10,000 threshold, so no lien is filed and no panel drawn. Note: the IRS's threshold (IRM 5.12.2) is on the aggregate unpaid balance; SLATE reads one year's. Even aggregated, her years stay far under it.

rows.player: Papers > Permission To Work > Social Security Number: Apply At The Social Security Office (an F-1 student, registered).

rows.timing: The card 21 days on (SLATE takes the longer end of SSA's two to three weeks).

rows.readers: hasSsn: bankmoves.ts channelFor (branch or online), identity.ts (Connecticut ID card), taxreturn.ts (the 1040-NR's W-7 and its seven weeks; the IRS plan online or by mail), Documents.tsx (the panel), lending.ts:458 (Discover asks for a number before its income test).

rows.gap: Behavior and evidence complete for every reader that changes an outcome in play (tests/evidence-g17-papers.test.ts: the panel rendered and pressed, the hour, the card's day, channelFor, the W-7's 21 against 70 days, the IRS plan online against by mail, the refusals; tests/defects-r7-1.test.ts: the ID card; tests/evidence3-lifepapers.test.ts: the hospital refusal by the week's draw). The lender reads it too, but Discover's $25,000-a-year wage test (wagesLastMonth, salary postings alone) is passed by no played life, need-based families included (scholarship isn't salary), so in play the number changes only which refusal Discover gives. The row's downstream claimed the lender as an outcome; that is a stale claim. Not done: no income invented and no eligibility loosened.
